title: feat(dissector): Add dissector for LDANeo device trailer
description:
This commit introduces a new Wireshark heuristic dissector for the
LDANeo device trailer. The dissector is registered to the `eth.trailer`
heuristic list and identifies the trailer by its unique signature ('L').

The 16-byte trailer contains metadata added by LDANeo devices, and this
dissector parses the following fields:

- A per-port sequence number.
- CRC validity status and a configurable device ID.
- Physical Coding Sublayer (PCS) information.
- Port details such as ID, speed (10G/25G/40G), and lane for 40G ports.
- An 80-bit high-precision timestamp with picosecond resolution.

Validation logic is included for port, speed, and PCS code fields to
ensure data integrity and flag malformed packets. The dissector also
provides an option to validate the timestamp against the packet's
capture time to improve detection accuracy.


For me this breaks the Windows build.

A cast would make sense!?

The Windows Arm64 builds are currently failing with

```
C:\gitlab-builds\builds\p9CfiwwBZ\0\wireshark\wireshark\epan\dissectors\packet-ldaneo.c(206,1): error C2055: expected formal parameter list, not a type list [C:\gitlab-builds\builds\p9CfiwwBZ\0\wireshark\wireshark\build\epan\dissectors\dissectors.vcxproj]
  extract_nstime(tvbuff_t *, int )
  ^
```

Can you take a look?
Never mind; Guy took care of it in !20645.

The next question after that is "why not use `_div128()` on ARM64?" The code currently tests for `defined(_M_X64) && (_MSC_VER >= 1920)`, but [the Microsoft documentation for `_div128()`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/intrinsics/div128?view=msvc-170) says nothing about it being x86-64-specific, although [the x86-64 intrinsics list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/intrinsics/x64-amd64-intrinsics-list?view=msvc-170) appears to be the only platform intrinsics list that includes it.

(And Google's AI hallucinated that the ARM64 list *does* include it, but, hey, [go catch a solid gold Magikarp](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/aPeJE8bSo6rAFoLqg/solidgoldmagikarp-plus-prompt-generation), Google AI - gotta catch 'em all!)

> The next question after that is "why not use `_div128()` on ARM64?"

And the answer is "Because Microsoft's compiler developers provide a bunch of platform-specific intrinsics, rather than being more GCC and LLVMish and defining platform-independent intrinsics that Do The Right Thing for each platform, even if there's no One Weird Instruction to do the job, and as there's no instruction to do 128/64 -> 64,64 on A32 or A64, we're not going to prove an intrinsic.".

Do you have a sample capture? I have some code taken from [c128](https://github.com/michaeljclark/c128) to do 128b/64b -> 64b, 64b division on platforms that don't have a compiler intrinsic that does it, and I'd like to test it.

The sample pcapng with picosecond timestamp resolution in #20608 is also a use case for 128 bit division and might be useful for your testing. (I solved the problem using some arithmetic around only needing to divide by powers of ten or powers of two, but 128 bit division would be easier to read, even if perhaps slower on some architectures.)

Here it is [picosec_sample.pcap](/uploads/056eb43bfeacf352956dd63ff43b8192/picosec_sample.pcap)

The capture contains one packet with LDANeo trailer and FCS.
